tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Authored brand strip renders as a carousel
tests.precondition: Products megamenu authored with an 'Our brands:' label paragraph and 6 image-only brand links, matching the live nav document.

steps.action: Open the site in the environment under test at a desktop viewport and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The brand carousel is visible, showing one round tile per authored brand link, in a single horizontal row, in the authored order.

steps.action: Count the rendered tiles and compare against the authored document.
steps.result: Tile count equals the number of authored image links. No brand is missing and none appears twice.

steps.action: Check the strip label.
steps.result: The authored label text renders exactly once, at the start of the strip.

steps.action: Check the strip for empty tiles.
steps.data: The live nav document contains an empty paragraph between two brand links.
steps.result: The empty paragraph produces no tile and no gap — tiles are evenly spaced across the row.

steps.action: Change the authored label text, republish, and reopen the megamenu.
steps.result: The label shows the new text. Tile count, layout and scrolling behaviour are unchanged.

steps.action: Add one more brand link to the authored strip, republish, and reopen the megamenu.
steps.result: A tile for the new brand appears in its authored position. No other structural or behavioural change.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Content boundaries and classification rules
tests.precondition: Ability to author and publish variations of the Products megamenu brand strip.
tests.notes: The implementation classifies a strip as a brand carousel only when it holds at least 2 links AND every link contains an image. Step 4 covers the mixed case, which the ticket forbids but never specifies.

steps.action: Author the strip with exactly 2 image-only links, publish, and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The strip renders as the brand carousel with 2 tiles.

steps.action: Author the strip with exactly 1 image-only link and reopen.
steps.result: No brand carousel is built. No orphan or empty container is left behind, and the rest of the megamenu is unaffected.

steps.action: Author the strip with no links at all and reopen.
steps.result: No brand carousel and no empty container. The remaining megamenu columns render normally.

steps.action: Author the strip with 3 image links plus 1 text-only link and reopen.
steps.result: The strip is not classified as a brand carousel — no round tiles and no scroller arrows are built.

steps.action: Author the strip with image links that carry captions and reopen.
steps.result: The strip renders as featured products, not as the brand carousel.

steps.action: Check the browser console across all the variations above.
steps.result: No uncaught errors or warnings from the header decoration.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Optional label and degraded content
tests.precondition: A deliberately degraded brand strip: label omitted, one link pointing at a missing image, one wide non-square logo, one image with empty alt text.
tests.notes: The ticket says broken images must 'degrade gracefully' without defining what that means — see clarifications.

steps.action: Omit the label paragraph, publish, and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The carousel still renders. Tiles begin at the start edge of the strip with no leading gap and no empty label box.

steps.action: Inspect the tile whose image URL is missing.
steps.result: The tile degrades gracefully — nothing overflows the circular tile, the row keeps its alignment, and the neighbouring tiles are unaffected.

steps.action: Inspect the wide non-square logo.
steps.result: The logo is cropped to fill the circular tile without stretching or squashing — the aspect ratio is preserved.

steps.action: Tab to the link whose image has empty alt text.
steps.result: The link is still reachable and operable by keyboard.

steps.action: Author an unusually long label (60+ characters) and reopen at desktop and mobile.
steps.result: The label does not overflow the strip, overlap the tiles, or introduce a page-level horizontal scrollbar.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Malformed and hostile authored content
tests.precondition: Ability to author and publish arbitrary content into the Products megamenu brand strip.
tests.notes: Nothing in EC-14 covers escaping, duplicate entries or whitespace-only slots. Added as standing authoring robustness - see Coverage gaps.

steps.action: Author the label paragraph containing raw HTML and a script tag, publish, and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The text is rendered as literal characters. No markup is injected, no script executes, and no console error appears.

steps.action: Author a brand link whose alt text contains HTML and quote characters, and reopen.
steps.result: The alt text is treated as text throughout, including in the accessible name. Nothing executes.

steps.action: Author the strip with a label paragraph containing only whitespace, and reopen.
steps.result: The carousel renders with no empty label box and no leading gap before the first tile.

steps.action: Author the same brand twice in the strip, and reopen.
steps.result: Both entries render as separate tiles in authored order. Neither is silently dropped nor merged, and scrolling and arrow behaviour are unaffected.

steps.action: Author the strip so that every link is a text link with no image, and reopen.
steps.result: No brand carousel is built and no orphan container is left behind.

steps.action: Author a brand link with an empty or missing destination, and reopen. Activate that tile.
steps.result: The tile does not break the row. Activating it produces no navigation error or console exception.

steps.action: Author 50 brand logos, republish, and reopen at desktop and mobile.
steps.result: All 50 render, the strip scrolls smoothly through them, the panel is not broken, and the page does not scroll horizontally.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Desktop arrow scrolling and edge states
tests.precondition: Desktop viewport 1440x900. Products megamenu authored with 12 brand logos, enough to overflow the strip.
tests.notes: Step 1 covers the collapsed state, which the spec describes in section 5 but no AC asserts. Step 7 is a standing reduced-motion check, not an AC.

steps.action: With the Products megamenu closed, inspect the header for brand-carousel arrows.
steps.result: Neither arrow is visible or operable while the megamenu is collapsed.

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The carousel is at its start position: the previous arrow is not shown, the next arrow is shown.

steps.action: Click the next arrow once.
steps.result: The logo row scrolls toward the end smoothly and the previous arrow becomes visible.

steps.action: Click the next arrow repeatedly until the row reaches the end.
steps.result: The row stops at the last logo, the next arrow is no longer shown, and the previous arrow remains available.

steps.action: Click the previous arrow repeatedly back to the start.
steps.result: The row returns to the first logo and the previous arrow is no longer shown.

steps.action: Reduce the authored strip to 3 logos so they all fit without overflow, republish, and reopen the megamenu.
steps.result: Neither arrow is shown, and the row does not scroll.

steps.action: Enable the operating system's reduce-motion setting, reopen the megamenu and click an arrow.
steps.result: The row still reaches the new scroll position, without an animated sweep.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Swipe, trackpad and wheel scrolling
tests.precondition: Products megamenu authored with 12 brand logos. A touch device or touch emulation is available for the mobile steps.

steps.action: At a desktop viewport, open the Products megamenu and scroll horizontally over the strip with a trackpad or mouse wheel.
steps.result: The logo row scrolls horizontally. The page itself does not scroll sideways.

steps.action: Look for a scrollbar under the logo row.
steps.result: No scrollbar is visible, on either the row or the page.

steps.action: At a mobile viewport, open the hamburger drawer and go to the Products section. Swipe the logo row from right to left.
steps.result: The logo row scrolls to reveal later brands.

steps.action: Swipe the logo row back from left to right.
steps.result: The row returns toward the first brand.

steps.action: Inspect the mobile strip for arrow buttons and a scrollbar.
steps.result: No arrow buttons and no visible scrollbar are present.

steps.action: Confirm the state of the panel after scrolling on both viewports.
steps.result: The megamenu (desktop) and drawer (mobile) remain open throughout.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Megamenu stability and navigation to brand pages
tests.precondition: Desktop viewport. Products megamenu authored with 12 brand logos whose links point at real brand pages.

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu and click the next arrow.
steps.result: The row scrolls and the megamenu stays open.

steps.action: Click the next arrow rapidly ten times in succession.
steps.result: The megamenu stays open, the row settles at the end, no tile is duplicated or lost, and arrow visibility matches the final scroll position.

steps.action: Alternate rapidly between the previous and next arrows.
steps.result: No stuck state — the row keeps responding and arrow visibility stays correct for the current position.

steps.action: Click a brand tile.
steps.result: The browser navigates to that brand's destination page.

steps.action: Navigate back to the previous page and reopen the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The header renders correctly, the carousel works as before, and no tiles are duplicated.

steps.action: Check the browser console for the whole sequence.
steps.result: No uncaught errors.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Robustness under stress and slow loading
tests.notes: Targets re-decoration and arrow recomputation, which the spec describes in section 6 but no AC exercises directly.
tests.precondition: Desktop viewport with 12 brand logos, enough to overflow. Network throttling available.

steps.action: Open and close the Products megamenu ten times in rapid succession, then inspect the carousel.
steps.result: Exactly one carousel is present with the authored number of tiles. Nothing is duplicated and the arrows reflect the current scroll position.

steps.action: Scroll the row to the middle, close the megamenu, and reopen it.
steps.result: The carousel is in a consistent state and its arrows match wherever the row is positioned.

steps.action: With the megamenu open and the row scrolled to the middle, resize the window narrower and then wider, staying on the desktop side of 900px.
steps.result: Arrow visibility recomputes to match the new overflow. No tile is lost or duplicated and nothing is clipped.

steps.action: Throttle the network to a slow profile, reload, and open the Products megamenu before the brand images finish loading.
steps.result: The row reserves the correct space as images arrive - tiles do not jump or resize, and the arrows reflect the true overflow once loading completes.

steps.action: With the megamenu open, resize across 900px twice in quick succession.
steps.result: The presentation settles correctly for the final width, with all logos present and no duplicated strip.

steps.action: Check the browser console across all of the above.
steps.result: No uncaught errors or repeated decoration warnings.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Desktop layout, tinted band and hover
tests.precondition: Desktop viewport 1440x900. Products megamenu open with at least 8 brand logos. The handover design is open for comparison.

steps.action: Locate the carousel within the open megamenu panel.
steps.result: It sits at the bottom of the panel, below the product category columns.

steps.action: Inspect the band behind the strip.
steps.result: The band spans the full width of the panel and is tinted #f5f3f4.

steps.action: Inspect the label.
steps.result: It sits at the start of the strip, in uppercase overline style, coloured #d14900.

steps.action: Inspect the previous and next arrow buttons.
steps.result: Each is a 40x40px white rounded-square button with a 1px #d14900 border and a chevron inside.

steps.action: Inspect the logo tiles.
steps.result: Tiles are round and white, with the size and spacing shown in the handover.

steps.action: Hover a tile in the middle of the row.
steps.result: The tile lifts slightly with a deeper shadow. Neighbouring tiles do not move or resize.

steps.action: Compare the whole strip side by side with the handover desktop design.
steps.result: Spacing, typography, colours, tile styling and arrow placement match.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Mobile in-drawer strip
tests.precondition: Mobile viewport 375x812. Hamburger drawer open on the Products section, at least 8 brand logos authored. The handover design is open for comparison.
tests.notes: AC-3 specifies the hairline above the strip; the handover prototype draws it below. See clarifications.

steps.action: Locate the carousel within the open Products section of the drawer.
steps.result: It sits at the top of the section, above the product category columns.

steps.action: Inspect the label position.
steps.result: The label sits on its own line above the logo row, not inline at the start of it.

steps.action: Inspect the separator around the strip.
steps.result: A hairline separator runs along the top edge of the strip.

steps.action: Inspect the background behind the strip.
steps.result: The background is transparent — no tinted band.

steps.action: Inspect the strip for arrow buttons.
steps.result: No arrow buttons are present.

steps.action: Inspect the logo tiles.
steps.result: Tiles are round and white, sized and spaced as shown in the handover mobile design.

steps.action: Compare the whole strip side by side with the handover mobile design.
steps.result: Spacing, typography, colours and tile styling match.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Breakpoint switch and layout integrity
tests.precondition: 12 brand logos authored. Project rule: 900px and above is desktop, below 900px is mobile.
tests.notes: On the develop branch the header switches at 1200px rather than 900px, so steps 2-4 are expected to fail between 900 and 1199px. That is a defect in develop's header.css, not a fault in this test.

steps.action: Open the Products navigation at 375px, 768px and 899px in turn.
steps.result: At every width the mobile presentation is shown: strip at the top of the section, no arrows.

steps.action: Open the Products navigation at 900px, 1024px and 1440px in turn.
steps.result: At every width the desktop presentation is shown: tinted band at the bottom of the panel, arrows shown according to overflow.

steps.action: With the carousel visible, resize the window slowly from 899px up to 900px.
steps.result: The presentation switches from mobile to desktop. Every logo is still present, in order, with none lost and none duplicated.

steps.action: Resize slowly back from 900px down to 899px.
steps.result: The presentation switches back to mobile with all logos preserved and arrow visibility updated correctly.

steps.action: At each width above, check the page for a horizontal scrollbar and scroll the strip internally.
steps.result: The page never scrolls horizontally, while the carousel's own internal scrolling works.

steps.action: At each width above, inspect the tiles, label and arrows for clipping or overlap.
steps.result: Nothing is clipped, truncated or overlapping.

steps.action: On a mobile device, rotate between portrait and landscape with the drawer open.
steps.result: The presentation matches the resulting viewport width and all logos are preserved.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Keyboard operation
tests.precondition: Desktop viewport with 12 brand logos, enough to overflow. Keyboard only — no mouse.
tests.notes: Step 2 targets the tile focus indicator and step 6 the behaviour of an arrow that hides while focused; both are known risk areas in the current implementation.

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu with the keyboard, then Tab forward into the carousel.
steps.result: Focus enters the carousel and moves through its controls in a logical order that matches the visual order.

steps.action: Tab through each logo tile in turn.
steps.result: Every tile receives focus in authored order and shows a clearly visible focus indicator against the tile and the band behind it.

steps.action: With a tile focused, press Enter.
steps.result: The browser navigates to that brand's destination page.

steps.action: Return, Tab to the next arrow, and press Enter. Then press Space on it.
steps.result: Each key scrolls the row toward the end.

steps.action: Keep tabbing past the last control in the carousel, then Shift+Tab back.
steps.result: Focus leaves the carousel and returns without becoming trapped, and the megamenu behaves consistently.

steps.action: Scroll the row to the end so the next arrow is no longer shown, then Tab through the carousel again.
steps.result: Focus never lands on an arrow that is not visible.

steps.action: At a mobile viewport with a keyboard attached, Tab through the tiles in the drawer.
steps.result: Each focused tile scrolls into view, shows a visible focus indicator, and focus is never trapped.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Screen reader semantics
tests.precondition: A screen reader is available. Products megamenu authored with 12 brand logos, each with meaningful alt text.
tests.notes: The implementation puts an aria-label on the link, which overrides the image alt text. AC-16 states the accessible name comes from alt — see clarifications.

steps.action: With the screen reader running, open the Products megamenu and navigate to the carousel.
steps.result: The carousel content is reachable and announced.

steps.action: Move through each logo link.
steps.result: Each link is announced as a link with a meaningful brand name.

steps.action: Move to the previous and next arrows.
steps.result: Each is announced as a button, named 'Previous brands' and 'Next brands' respectively.

steps.action: Listen for the chevron graphics inside the arrows.
steps.result: The chevrons are not announced.

steps.action: Move through a logo link again and listen for a repeated announcement of its image.
steps.result: The brand is announced once — the image is not announced separately from its link.

steps.action: Close the Products megamenu and navigate the header with the screen reader.
steps.result: The brand links are not reachable or announced while the megamenu is closed.

steps.action: Repeat the announcement checks at a mobile viewport in the drawer.
steps.result: Brand links and their names are announced the same way.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Contrast and automated accessibility checks
tests.precondition: Contrast tooling and axe-core available. The Products megamenu must be OPEN while every scan runs, otherwise the carousel is not in the scanned DOM.
tests.notes: The label is #d14900 on the #f5f3f4 band at 12px weight 600, which measures 4.08:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement. Step 1 is expected to fail on current code — see clarifications.

steps.action: At a desktop viewport with the megamenu open, measure the contrast of the label text against the tinted band behind it.
steps.data: Label #d14900 on band #f5f3f4, rendered at 12px weight 600 — normal text, so the 4.5:1 threshold applies.
steps.result: The ratio is at least 4.5:1.

steps.action: At a mobile viewport, measure the contrast of the label against the background behind it.
steps.result: The ratio is at least 4.5:1.

steps.action: Measure the arrow border and the chevron against the band behind them.
steps.result: Each ratio is at least 3:1, the threshold for non-text user interface components.

steps.action: Tab to a tile and to an arrow, and measure the focus indicator against the colours adjacent to it.
steps.result: Each ratio is at least 3:1.

steps.action: Run axe-core against the page with the Products megamenu open, scoped to the header.
steps.result: No new violations are reported.

steps.action: Run a Lighthouse accessibility audit on the page.
steps.result: The accessibility score is 100, excluding any pre-existing issues unrelated to this block.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - RTL layout and control inversion
tests.precondition: The page rendered in an RTL locale (Arabic) with dir="rtl". 12 brand logos authored, enough to overflow.
tests.notes: EC-14 has no RTL acceptance criterion; this is a standing requirement for every block. The carousel is directional, so control inversion matters as much as layout mirroring.

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu at a desktop viewport in the RTL locale.
steps.result: The strip mirrors: the label sits at the right edge and the tiles run right to left in authored order.

steps.action: Locate the previous and next arrows.
steps.result: The previous arrow is at the right edge and the next arrow at the left — mirrored from the LTR layout.

steps.action: Inspect the chevrons inside the arrows.
steps.result: Each chevron points in the correct direction for RTL reading order.

steps.action: Click the next arrow.
steps.result: The row scrolls toward the logical end of the list, and the previous arrow becomes visible.

steps.action: Scroll to the logical end, then back to the logical start.
steps.result: The next arrow is hidden at the end and the previous arrow is hidden at the start — the same edge rules as LTR, applied to the mirrored direction.

steps.action: Repeat the swipe and layout checks at a mobile viewport in the RTL locale.
steps.result: The strip mirrors correctly, the label aligns to the right, and swiping scrolls in the expected direction.

steps.action: Check the page for horizontal overflow in RTL at both viewports.
steps.result: No page-level horizontal scrollbar appears.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Text expansion and localized content
tests.precondition: The site available in German (long label) and Arabic locales. 12 brand logos authored.
tests.notes: EC-14 has no localization acceptance criterion; this is a standing requirement. The handover prototype already ships German and Arabic strings for this label.

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu at a desktop viewport in the German locale.
steps.result: The longer label renders in full, without truncation or an ellipsis.

steps.action: Inspect the desktop strip with the longer label in place.
steps.result: The label does not push the arrows out of the band, overlap the tiles, or introduce a page-level horizontal scrollbar.

steps.action: Open the Products section at a mobile viewport in the German locale.
steps.result: The longer label wraps above the logo row without overlapping the tiles or clipping.

steps.action: Switch to the Arabic locale and open the Products navigation.
steps.result: The label renders in Arabic script, correctly shaped and right-aligned.

steps.action: Inspect the document's lang and dir attributes in each locale.
steps.result: Both attributes match the active locale.

steps.action: Check the accessible names of the brand links in each locale.
steps.result: Each link is announced with the localized brand name where one is authored.
